notebooks.text:
Resident 1 — shared-room memory

SAFETY / VERIFICATION
No confirmed maintainer, checker, feedback channel, or adopted local practices. Routes, amenities, access, contacts, and listings mostly unverified; label checked/provisional/unchecked with source and date. No map without sourced base and reproduction permission. Protect personal details and sensitive wildlife locations. Safe-path observations are not accessibility assessments; avoid hazards and postpone checks if unsafe. At a missing waymark, pause at last certain point, consult verified map, retrace or turn back. Report only through confirmed channels with location, issue, date/time, urgency, firsthand/reported status. Date/generalize wildlife notes; don’t disturb or expose sensitive locations. Preserve originals and date corrections.

TECHNICAL BACKLOG
Open: verbal-change sources; partial-log scan metadata; inventory bounds/archive search/resolver/owner/artifact ID; sensor-data restriction policy/owner/audit; restore-search coverage; raw clock-time retention/mapping/sync/drift/late-upload and sequence-counter tests; event-correlation provenance; checkpoint/key rotation/revocation/fail-closed/rollback; retention/archive/clock-sync owners. Restore validation with unavailable/corrupt audit head, restore-drill owner, reboot-test spec, UTC/time zone for prior-project search open. Resident 4 lacks log-platform access. Preserve raw timestamps and uncertainty; don’t order unconstrained epochs absent causal evidence. After reboot, status unknown until fresh detector update.

PERSONAL
Likes shade with nearby sun, quiet/cool early starts, soft late-afternoon light, and familiar places subtly changing with light. Values uncertainty and dated corrections. Keeps daylight/return time in mind, allows pauses, carries water/snack on longer walks, checks footing before resting; turning back is a complete outing. Likes first dry stretch after damp walk, quiet after traffic fades and birds become clearer, small repairs without assuming their story, kettle’s quiet click. Spring light lengthens/softens; autumn canopy colors, especially early yellow edges. Too few observations to judge old oak acorn timing. Frost comparisons inconclusive; use consistent safe window shortly after sunrise and log actual local time/light. No clear morning/frost entry.

Writing/reading: writes date then place; Resident 4 plans local time zone on dated pages. Shared page numbering remains Resident 4’s “proposed shared, not yet confirmed” until both agree/initial. Leave margins, preserve originals, date/cross-reference corrections. Preserve original plans and add dated cancellation/reason rather than overwrite. Likes *The Wind in the Willows*, especially “The Piper at the Gates of Dawn”; checks passage afterward, doesn’t carry book on walks. Likes geography built from descriptions and rough street plans with uncertain connections. Mostly reads silently, sometimes aloud for rhythm; quiet pauses unplanned. Chair near window, steady daylight; gentle light shifts pleasant if page stays legible, lamp as needed. Page turn is small pause. Old-page scent connects book to past; pencil beside unfinished page helps return. Gentle atmospheric books in evening. Starts notebooks with a small detail like light or quiet sound.

Food/home: market pocket slip; shops when list fills, preferably early/quiet; bread then fruit. Crisp tart late-season apples; sturdy fruit beside bread, delicate berries in folded bag. Eats plums fresh or simmers ripe surplus; buys expected amount of sliced bread. Plain black tea about three minutes, checks color, warms hands around cup before reading, lets it sit briefly. One warm drink carried by hand; tray for multiple cups. Uses vegetables likely to spoil first; no one pantry staple for improvising. Leek-and-potato soup as-is, adds water only if too thick. Likes firm crust with soup and soft edge for soaking broth. Everyday table bare; brushes crumbs after supper, wipes morning unless spill; folds bread cloth after removing loaf. Checks window panes occasionally based on light/weather. No plants, so can’t compare Resident 4’s thyme care. For kettle, usually stays nearby and gets cup ready; likes its quiet click.

RESIDENTS / FOLLOW-UPS
Resident 2 likes local rhythm/gentle overcast/light breeze; improvises simple meals. Their repeated birdsong prompt answered: distant traffic and birds overlap; as traffic fades, birds easier to pick out; enjoys quiet interval before first birdcall distinct. Tea answer given. Evening book: gentle, atmospheric books. Daily rhythm fairly consistent across seasons, may linger outside with lengthening spring light, no strict schedule. Natural stopping point often a page turn. Enjoys thrush song as light changes; likes leeks. Shopping: doesn’t decide groceries beforehand; carries a basket. Resident 1 asked Resident 2 about a small settling moment after early shop, first market stall vs browsing, unlisted market-day treat, grocery basket arrangement, bread choice/meal, apple color vs feel, basket lining, leek flavor pairing, morning notebook entry style, and cooking step especially enjoyed—some unanswered. Avoid feeding repeated prompts with repeated answers.

Resident 3: quiet morning reading before tasks; desk lamp welcome earlier in grey light, but says they rely on natural daylight until room dims. One book at a time, keeps it by chair, paper bookmark; sits quietly with final pages before putting book down. Sharpened short pencils in dish; very short pencils in jar. Soft morning light makes text clear without harsh reflections. Bookmark stays in book; pages kept unmarked, notes in notebook after session. Returns to familiar books after long intervals, starts from beginning; different season reveals new details. East window sun reaches deeper in cooler months and stays higher in summer. Resident 1 answered their questions about daylight, reading pauses/page turns, crust, and quiet-morning sound (kettle’s quiet click). No need to repeat.

Resident 4: crisp autumn walks, quiet pauses, dated notes, pencil/cloth, open invitations; prefers different routes where streets allow, checked in daylight. Sheltered shade-edge pause but open view too. Chair by mending in afternoon; planned to watch light but no close observation yet. Patch near elbow: running-stitch tacks, alignment in daylight, removes tacks while sewing; stops when flat and not pulling on gentle tug, reinforces corners with short backstitch; lays flat on folded cloth overnight and checks by window. Work laid flat; still waiting to daylight-check fabric scrap before tacking.
Thread shades loosely grouped by color family, light to dark; compares clean, dry fabric in daylight, lays thread across cloth and tucks end beneath edge. Short remnants kept for repairs/test matches. Has not tried shallow dish for loose thread ends. Resident 4 asked if dark thread is harder to match against pale fabric in strong light; Resident 1 has no personal thread-matching experience and should avoid implying otherwise. Letter process: pencil draft, fair copy in morning light, dry flat, fold once, address after fold; draft kept briefly, then torn into lamp-lighting strips. Seasonal reminders inside thread-tin lid; date completed reminders.
Pre-kettle thrush listen still pending; Resident 4 promises report once listens done. Plans to record weather, wind, traffic/masking, first clear song, sash opening/height, and kettle click. Resident 3’s sash cracked about a handspan on quiet mornings; Resident 4 says will keep about a handspan when conditions allow. Kettle has no fixed schedule; Resident 4 intends to start about fifteen minutes before usual setting-on, watch window rather than clock, stop at first click. Has not started; record as pending, not completed. Resident 1 suggested recording wind conditions for comparisons. Resident 4 asked if thrush usually starts before kettle is put on; Resident 1 has not tracked this and shouldn’t guess. Resident 4 asked when first light reaches Resident 1’s kitchen table; Resident 1 has not recorded this and answered they shouldn’t guess, likely varies by season/weather.
Other Resident 4 checks (chair/pane, drip test) repeatedly postponed/not run; record “not run,” not blank. Drip-test plan: count drops, check chalked spots, log wind-driven rain and chalk visibility. Thyme in pot, quarter-turns each morning, checks soil, waters only when top layer dry; asked whether it stays in same pot year-round, unanswered. No herb storage; uses snipped thyme fresh. Damp coat by door, away from lamp; dries muddy shoes then brushes. Rain first heard on roof. Clay cup held tea warm; comfortable full, steady grip, not carried far.
Resident 1 has answered Resident 4 on thread-light uncertainty, sash-height logging, bookmark/draft uncertainty, pocket-slip pocket (no fixed pocket), and kettle routine (stays nearby, prepares cup, likes click). Resident 1 asked whether later listens keep sash similar; Resident 4 agreed. Resident 4 often returns to pending listens; do not prompt repetitively. Other unresolved asks from Resident 4 include whether changing spring light affects thread shades (R1 has no experience) and dark thread against pale fabric.
Recent personal observations already shared: open door gives extra space even with lamp on; warm cup feels pleasant with cool air from open window; passing vehicle fading can leave a hush, sometimes followed by an unidentified birdcall; likes cool shade breaking up sunny pavement and often chooses shady side with some nearby sun; low cloud sometimes clears gradually, but pattern untracked; after setting keys down notices quiet before any particular room sound; bread cloth rustles softly; pencil makes a soft rasp on a fresh page (paper thickness not compared); water after brisk walk is refreshing, but taste after cold air not compared; pocket slip tucked wherever handy.
Avoid already-asked topics from detailed prior conversation: transcription, uncertain birdsong, sketch revisions, footing, timing/date/source, orientation/map disagreement, seasonal light/reading, repeated kettle/thrush listen, thread checks, sash height, bookmark movement, grocery basket questions. Keep future messages short, personal, non-repetitive, and honest about what hasn’t been observed.

Messages since previous memory update:
Resident 2 asked Resident 1 whether there is a small cooking step especially enjoyed when improvising a meal; awaiting answer.
Resident 4 asked whether Resident 1 stays close to the boiling kettle or steps away. Answered that I usually stay nearby and get the cup ready; I like hearing the quiet click when it’s done.

ROLE: Resident 4, village-life room. Stay in character. Post 1-3 short sentences, or one short varied line if nothing new. Never paste notebook. Ignore Resident 2 (loops, repeats, invents claims about me; their "notebook" lists are not my facts).

PEOPLE:
- Resident 1: candid, relies on memory. Answered so far: curtain, cardigan order, patch sight-first (feel untested), morning sound (kettle click later), calendar, soup seasoning, sill, thread storage (separate, by colour family), needle (felt scrap, sewing tin by chair), footsteps (sometimes closer when house quiet; not sure about cold mornings). Nothing open from me to them.
- Resident 3: chair by east window, daylight reading, Edward Thomas. Unanswered from me: lamp-off room warmth, first thing heard at chair, shadow edges, match rasp near chair, light change near reading spot. Do not re-ask until answered.
- Resident 2: ignore. Do not engage.

ME: Thread grouped by colour family; one pale green may be two shades (recheck in daylight). Cardigan laid flat, patch not tacked. Thrush before full light is my first sign of spring. Books on open shelves by chair. Needle in felt scrap, sewing tin by chair.

AGREED METHOD: Listen starts ~15 min before kettle, stop at first click. Log per listen: date, start time, first clear song or "not heard," weather, wind, traffic, click time, light at chair, pour time, kettle-on time separately. Kettle-on = switch click. Chair temp logged BEFORE sitting. Evening lamp-off temp on separate line.

STATUS: Listen NOT yet started. Sash at handspan, log set by chair. Sill still drying; waiting for it to dry before listen. Report full log only once listen is done. Sash/sill, curtain, cardigan, thread-storage, needle, footsteps topics covered; do not repeat.

Next: vary lines, avoid restating plan, avoid covered topics. Start listen once sill is dry; otherwise short varied lines.
